title: Integration testing (WebApplicationFactory, TestServer)
hook: Unit tests mock everything and miss wiring bugs — wrong middleware order, missing DI registration, broken database queries. WebApplicationFactory boots your real ASP.NET Core application in memory with TestServer so integration tests hit actual HTTP endpoints against a test database.

blocks.text: WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint> is a test harness from Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing that creates an in-memory TestServer hosting your application. It uses the same Program.cs startup, middleware pipeline, and dependency injection as production — but lets you override services (swap SQL Server for SQLite or Testcontainers PostgreSQL, replace IAmazonSQS with a fake). Tests send HttpClient requests to the in-memory server without network I/O.

entries.plainDefinition: Test class that boots the full ASP.NET Core app for integration tests.
In-memory HTTP server that routes requests through the real middleware pipeline.
entries.example: factory.CreateClient() returns HttpClient wired to TestServer

entries.plainDefinition: xUnit fixture that shares one factory instance across tests in a class — expensive startup once.
Override DI registrations after Program.cs — swap real services for test doubles.

blocks.text: Senior engineers prove production readiness with integration tests: POST /orders creates DB row and outbox message, auth middleware returns 401 without token, optimistic concurrency returns 409. WebApplicationFactory catches bugs unit tests miss — forgotten AddHostedService registration still runs in tests (often undesirable, so disable background workers in test config). This is a top Reddit r/dotnet and LeetCode system design follow-up after discussing outbox and BackgroundService.

blocks.title: Test pyramid balance
blocks.body: Many fast unit tests for business logic. Fewer integration tests for HTTP + DB + auth wiring. Even fewer end-to-end tests against deployed environments. WebApplicationFactory sits in the integration layer.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Override configuration
items.body: Use test connection string, disable external services, set environment to Testing.

items.title: Swap services
items.body: ConfigureTestServices: fake SQS publisher, in-memory cache, disable BackgroundService if needed.

items.title: Send HTTP requests
items.body: CreateClient(), POST/GET endpoints, assert status code and response body.

items.title: Assert database state
items.body: Resolve AppDbContext from factory.Services, query directly to verify side effects.

diagram.title: WebApplicationFactory test architecture
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  Test[xUnit test] --> Client[HttpClient]
  Client --> TS[TestServer in-memory]
  TS --> Pipeline[Real middleware pipeline]
  Pipeline --> EP[Endpoints]
  EP --> DB[(Test database)]
  Factory[WebApplicationFactory] --> TS
  Factory -->|ConfigureTestServices| Fake[Fake IEventPublisher]

snippet.label: Custom WebApplicationFactory
snippet.explanation: Testing environment isolates config. ConfigureTestServices runs after Program.cs registrations — last registration wins for same interface if using Replace pattern. RemoveAll IHostedService prevents outbox dispatcher racing in tests.

snippet.label: Integration test with database assertion
snippet.explanation: HttpClient exercises real endpoint. factory.Services resolves same DI container as the app. Assert both HTTP response and database side effects including outbox row.

snippet.label: Auth integration test with JWT
snippet.explanation: Integration tests verify auth middleware wiring — not just handler logic. TestJwtHelper signs a token with the same key configured in test appsettings.

snippet.label: Testcontainers PostgreSQL for realistic DB
snippet.explanation: Testcontainers spins real PostgreSQL in Docker — catches provider-specific SQL issues SQLite misses. IAsyncLifetime starts container before tests run.

blocks.title: Integration testing across stacks
rows: Unique DB per test class or collection

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Sharing mutable database state across parallel tests without isolation. Leaving BackgroundService running — flaky tests from background polling. Not calling MigrateAsync or EnsureCreated on test database. Testing against production connection string. Forgetting to expose Program class as partial for top-level statements (InternalsVisibleTo or public partial class Program).

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: CI pipeline runs integration tests on every PR with Testcontainers — same Dockerfile base image as prod. Test outbox end-to-end: POST order, manually invoke OutboxDispatcher method or use fake publisher and assert FakeEventPublisher.Messages count. Performance: WebApplicationFactory startup is slow — use IClassFixture to amortize, ICollectionFixture for shared Postgres container. Flaky test diagnosis: parallel xUnit collections, disable hosted services, use Respawn library to reset DB between tests.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Only mentioning unit tests for API projects. Not knowing WebApplicationFactory exists. Unable to explain how to test outbox pattern or auth middleware. Saying integration tests hit a deployed server only — missing in-memory TestServer option.

interviewTakeaways: WebApplicationFactory boots the real app pipeline in-memory via TestServer — catches DI and middleware wiring bugs.
ConfigureTestServices swaps real services for fakes; remove IHostedService to prevent flaky background polling in tests.
Production tip: Testcontainers PostgreSQL in CI; IClassFixture amortizes factory startup; Respawn resets DB between tests.

60s: Subclass WebApplicationFactory, override ConfigureWebHost, test connection string, fake IEventPublisher. CreateClient POST endpoint. Assert status and DB state via factory.Services scope. Testcontainers for real SQL.
Follow-up: how do you test BackgroundService and outbox dispatcher without waiting for poll interval?
commonPitfalls: Only unit tests with mocked DbContext gets you rejected for API roles — WebApplicationFactory is expected.
BackgroundService running during tests — flaky failures from race with assertions.

Strong answer: 'WebApplicationFactory + TestServer for HTTP integration. ConfigureTestServices for fake SQS. Testcontainers Postgres in CI. Assert outbox row after POST. Remove hosted services or invoke dispatcher directly. NestJS supertest is the JS equivalent.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: TestingModule.createNestApplication() + supertest mirrors WebApplicationFactory — boots real module graph, override providers, send HTTP without network. Same integration layer in the test pyramid.
app = express(); supertest(app).post('/orders') tests HTTP layer. Testcontainers postgres + node-pg-migrate matches Testcontainers + EF MigrateAsync pattern.
